hero.title: Axonpack ends the guesswork
hero.lead: Answers you and your agent can both read. Every request, error, log and stored value, captured on the device and copied out as structured JSON.

usage.title: One provider, one flag
usage.body: No client to create and pass around, and no init call to place correctly. Wrap the app once, configure it inline or from a file, and one flag decides whether any of it runs.
usage.note: The patches go in as the provider renders, so the first screen is already covered, and nothing records anywhere unless enabled says so.

principles.title: How they are built
principles.body: The point of a foundation library is that you stop thinking about it. These are what keep them that way.

items.title: Small and focused
items.body: One package solves one problem. Nothing here grows into a framework that wants to own your app's structure.

items.title: Dependency-light
items.body: Adding a package should not add a supply chain. Where one needs a library you may already have, you hand it over rather than having it installed for you.

items.title: Independently published
items.body: Each package versions and ships on its own, with its own documentation. Installing one never drags in another.

items.title: Honest about limits
items.body: Every guide ends with what the thing cannot do, and why. A number that cannot be measured is not shown rather than invented.

showcase.title: It runs on the device
showcase.body: This is not a socket to a desktop window. The panel is part of the app, so it works on a real phone, over a tunnel, and in a release build you deliberately left it in.
